NetSuite remains the system of record: NetSuite holds your customers, stock and invoices. What we hold is the guide for each kitchen, priced and kept up to date by you, and the orders placed through our app.

Kitchens already ordering online carry on: If some accounts already use the NetSuite store, leave them there. The app is meant for the kitchens that keep phoning. An order phoned to your office gets no number from us; only the ones sent from the app do.

Getting started adds nothing to your NetSuite license: NetSuite's license grows with each module you add, and online ordering for customers is one of them. Starting with us adds no NetSuite module and no NetSuite user. Whether EDI or the API comes later is a question for the demo. We send our own quote, separate from NetSuite's.

review.reviewBody: I used to spend hours every week ordering food. Now it's simple, super easy, and I have free time to spend on other aspects of my restaurant.

@graph.name: Three steps, with NetSuite left as it is
@graph.description: It starts with one export from NetSuite. We turn it into a guide for each account, and the kitchens take it from there.

step.name: Pull an item list out of NetSuite
step.text: A saved search exported to a spreadsheet is usually all we need. It gives us each account's items and prices under your own codes.

step.name: Every account gets its own guide
step.text: We build each guide and open the account, and the kitchen installs the app. Most place a first order the same day.

step.name: Your desk gets a ready order
step.text: Each order arrives already checked by the customer, numbered and timed, in the format you chose.

@graph.name: Do we need a NetSuite alternative to take voice orders from kitchens?

acceptedAnswer.text: No. NetSuite carries on running your business, and the store can stay for the accounts that use it. What we add is an app for your phone-ordering kitchens: they say what they need, review it and send it, with no new NetSuite module.

@graph.name: Is VoiceOrder Solutions better than NetSuite?

acceptedAnswer.text: At one job, yes: getting an order out of a kitchen that will not sign in to any website, with each line looked over first. NetSuite does far more than we do, which is why we sit beside it rather than in its place.

@graph.name: NetSuite already sells a store. Why would we want an app too?

acceptedAnswer.text: Keep the store for anyone who already orders there. It is built for finding items and typing quantities. Our app is for kitchens that find saying what they need easier than looking each item up.

@graph.name: NetSuite partners sell voice tools. How is this different?

acceptedAnswer.text: Several partners do, mostly for sales reps, or for turning voice notes and calls into sales orders. Our app is in the customer's hands instead: the kitchen orders out loud, then checks each line before it is sent to you.

@graph.name: Will someone still have to type these orders into NetSuite?

acceptedAnswer.text: These are two products with nothing joining them out of the box, and neither of us gives support for the other's software. Through EDI or the API, NetSuite may accept the order without anyone retyping it, if your account is set up for that; we check it with you in the demo. By email, it is a file the kitchen reviewed before sending, and someone on your side keys it in from that file rather than from a call or a voicemail.

@graph.name: Will setting this up touch our NetSuite account?

acceptedAnswer.text: Getting started needs no NetSuite login and installs nothing: we work from a spreadsheet you export, and your scripts, roles and release schedule stay as they are. If you later want orders sent by EDI or the API, we go through what that takes for you in the demo.

@graph.name: How long does it take, and what does it cost?

acceptedAnswer.text: Setup takes 24 to 48 hours for most distributors, with nothing changed inside NetSuite. Neither company publishes prices, so both are quoted: NetSuite's license and ours. A NetSuite replacement, or any NetSuite alternative that takes over the ERP, moves your finance, stock and warehouse at once. Changing how kitchens send orders is a job of a different size.
